Class ContributorTestingAutomation

java.lang.Object
automationTestbed.ContributorTestingAutomation
public class ContributorTestingAutomation extends Object

Tests creating, reading, updating, deleting, and listing lessons learned as per our user stories Also removes test records after running, except for one kept to test persistence between runs.

Version:
1.0
Author:
Manuel Dominguez

    • runNormalTests

    • testCreateLessons

      private static void testCreateLessons()

      Creates lessons. tests involve valid, missing, duplicate, and max length input, then checks against the database results

      Purpose: These tests check the user story that a Contributor can add a lesson with core information. Test 1 checks that the title and description are actually saved to the database with the author and a unique ID. Tests 2 and 3 check that required core information cannot be left empty. Test 4 tests unique title rules we implemented, and makes sure a rejected duplicate does not replace the original lesson. Tests 5 and 6 checks the description's 1600 character limit, the full allowed amount must save, and an extra character must be rejected. And a negative case passes when the input is rejected and nothing is saved or changed.

    • testReadLessons

      private static void testReadLessons()

      tests the reading of lesson details and checks both matching and empty lesson list subsets.

      Purpose: These tests check the lesson data needed for the story that a Contributor can list lessons and choose one to examine. Test 7 checks that selecting an existing lesson by ID returns the expected saved information from the database. Test 8 checks that a missing ID does not return any lesson. Test 9 checks that the loaded list and a matching subset contain the intended lesson, and test 10 checks that an unmatched search gives an empty subset. Passing means the returned information or absence matches the expected result.

    • testUpdateLessons

      private static void testUpdateLessons()

      testing updates to the title and description, then checks that empty field updates leave the saved lesson unchanged.

      Purpose: These tests check the story that a Contributor can manage a lesson after adding it. Test 11 checks that changing the title only keeps the same lesson ID, description, and author. Test 12 checks that changing the description only keeps the other information. Tests 13 and 14 check that trying to clear either required field does not damage the existing lesson. Reading the lesson back confirms that valid edits were stored and invalid edits left all fields unchanged.

    • testDeleteLessons

      private static void testDeleteLessons()

      Deletes a lesson, checks that it is gone, and tries deleting it again

      Purpose: These tests check deletion as part of managing a lesson. Test 15 checks that the deleted lesson cannot still be retrieved from the database or found in the refreshed list. Test 16 checks that trying to delete it again is rejected instead of reporting another successful deletion. Passing requires the correct return value and the lesson to remain absent.

    • testAuthorLessonList

      private static void testAuthorLessonList()

      Checks the database can lists lesson titles for an author, ordered by lesson ID.

      Purpose: These tests support the stories that a Contributor can list their own lessons and cannot see submissions from other Contributors. Test 17 creates lessons for two authors, then checks that the requested author's list contains both of their lessons and none from the other author. The titles are in opposite alphabetical order so the test also checks our database's ID ordering. Test 18 checks that an author with no lessons receives an empty list instead of someone else's lessons or an error. Passing requires the exact expected list.

    • testPersistence

      private static void testPersistence()

      Checks for the persistence lesson saved by a previous execution. If not exists, attempts to create it and asks the user to run the tests again for the persistence check.

      Purpose: This test checks the database's persistent storage so a lesson added by a Contributor remains available after the program closes. The first run creates a dedicated lesson and leaves it saved within the database. Test 19 on a later run checks if the lesson by title exists, then checks its title, description, author, and positive ID for any edit or missing values since the last run. Passing means those saved values are still available from a separate execution. Creating the record on the first run only prepares this check and is not counted as proof of persistence.
